constraint: In binocular rivalry, frontal fMRI activity relates to reporting switches, not to the switches themselves.
The cerebellum holds most of the brain's neurons, yet losing it impairs movement and not, as far as anyone reports, consciousness.
Wakefulness and awareness dissociate: patients in the vegetative / unresponsive wakefulness state open their eyes and have sleep-wake cycles without behavioural signs of awareness.
Large prefrontal lesions do not abolish consciousness.
Stimulating lateral prefrontal cortex seldom changes experience; orbitofrontal and anterior cingulate stimulation often does.
Anaesthetic-dose ketamine makes people unresponsive, yet they report long vivid dreams afterwards, and their TMS-EEG complexity stays wake-like; propofol and xenon give low complexity and no reports.
Within both NREM and REM, dream reports follow a local drop in low-frequency EEG power over posterior cortex; high-frequency activity there tracks specific contents.
The P3b disappears when people see a stimulus but do not have to report it; it tracks report and task relevance, not awareness.
Prefrontal neurons in macaques track the content of rivalry switches with no report, enough to decode contents single-trial.
Children born without most of the cerebral cortex (hydranencephaly) show emotional and orienting responses that some clinicians read as conscious.
